newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NEW S.AFRICAN PARLIAMENT STRUCTURE WILL COST.
newsitem.headline: NEW S.AFRICAN PARLIAMENT STRUCTURE WILL COST.

text.p: The creation of a new parliamentary body in South Africa dealing with provincial affairs will involve substantial costs, parliamentary speaker Frene Ginwala said on Wednesday.
Under the new constitution a National Council of Provinces will replace the senate from this year.
The council is intended to give the nine provinces a voice in national legislation that affects them and will involve the provinces sending delegates to parliament in Cape Town.
"There are additions, some of which have not been costed. For example, provinces will establish offices in parliament," Ginwala told a news conference.

"We need a very good communication system...We're going to have to refer legislation to nine provincial legislatures. We're looking at a computer system linking the provincial legislatures and the national legislature...I could not give you a figure, but I do know it will be a substantial amount," she said.
"It's only when the council starts functioning that we will have a realistic assessment of what the actual budget implications are."
Parliamentary officials said the work of the new council could entail a good deal of extra travelling to and from Cape Town for provincial delegates.
They said some provinces had complained that Cape Town was relatively inaccessible and that it would be more convenient to have the national assembly in Gauteng province.
